subject.title: fix(exec): read legacy exec-approvals.json instead of deny fallback (#93518)

question: Should OpenClaw trust an unmigrated legacy `~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json` file at runtime when `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` points elsewhere and the canonical state-dir approvals file is absent?
rationale: The branch fixes a real denial path, but the remaining choice changes the exec authorization security boundary and repository migration contract; automation cannot safely choose that policy.

options.title: Keep migration-first fail-closed behavior
options.body: Preserve the runtime fallback as deny/always and repair startup or doctor migration so valid legacy approvals are copied into the canonical state-dir file before policy resolution.

options.title: Accept runtime legacy trust
options.body: Allow the runtime to read legacy approvals directly, but require explicit security rationale plus tests for stale, invalid, symlinked, blocked-migration, and no-target-file states.

options.title: Pause for alternate root cause
options.body: Hold this branch if maintainers believe the user-visible denial is better solved in node policy or approved-marker handling instead of exec approval migration.

recommendation.title: Keep migration-first fail-closed behavior
recommendation.body: Preserve the runtime fallback as deny/always and repair startup or doctor migration so valid legacy approvals are copied into the canonical state-dir file before policy resolution.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle authored and merged the state-dir approvals migration and is the clearest history owner for the fallback versus migration contract.
